transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

No — a displayed 3:39 on Eco 40-60 is normally expected, not a reason by itself to return the machine. Eco programmes are designed to use less energy by washing at lower temperatures for longer, and the displayed time can alter as the machine assesses the load, foam and spin balance. Your previous one-hour 40°C wash was likely a standard or quick programme rather than the current Eco cycle. The important distinction is whether it completes: if it finishes normally, this is normal operation. If the timer repeatedly adds time, resets, never completes, or shows an error code, then it needs investigating and, as it is newly bought, the retailer/manufacturer should deal with it under warranty.

It does finish and spin fine, and the clothes come out clean. It's just that the time is 3:39 every time on Eco 40-60, and the Cottons 40 is only about 2 hours. Is there anything I can do to make it shorter, or is that just how it is?

That is just how Eco 40-60 is intended to run: 3:39 is a normal Eco duration, while roughly two hours for Cottons 40 is the shorter everyday alternative. Eco 40-60 is the energy-label programme, so its long low-energy wash is deliberate rather than a fault. As it finishes, spins and cleans properly, there is no reason to return the machine for this.

candidates: Cycle-time adjustment for load, foam or balance (medium)
